conviction_note: FY26 revenue, margin, leverage and the 'in line' FY27 steer were all pre-released on 22 Oct, so the results-day move rests on what is still new: the promised capital-return detail and the new CEO's first FY27 outlook. Both land in the middle of a requisitioned-meeting fight (GM 7 Dec) in which the board needs a strong results day. That gives a mild upward lean (p_up 56) on a move sized above the pre-released base (abs 5.0). The findings sum to +1.2, double the scaled +0.6, because the capital-return finding is sized as a likely positive on its own, while p_up carries the real chance that the return disappoints in size or form. A buyback needs shareholder authority, and FitzWalter can block it.

findings.finding: The FY26 results will carry the board's first concrete excess-capital return. The company itself said so on 22 Oct with leverage at c.1.5x, the trigger it set in May. A board defending itself at a 7 Dec requisitioned GM has every incentive to make the return meaningful. FitzWalter has publicly called for a buyback, so a sizeable return also undercuts its campaign.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $40m buyback launched in 2025 was ended after $16.5m (per FitzWalter's members' statement); no return announcement has been made under the current leverage trigger. No observed results-day reaction to a capital-return surprise on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The market knows a return is coming but not its size or form, and the stock has slipped 15% since 5 Nov (508p to 430p on 20 Nov, 442p on 23 Nov) with no RNS. A market already crediting a large return would not have drifted down into the print. If it had priced the return, the price would sit near the 5 Nov high, where the 26 Oct requisition and strategic-review hopes had taken it. The form is constrained in a way the headline does not show: market-purchase authority failed at the Jan 2026 AGM (Resolution 17, 73.78% for against a 75% threshold), so a buyback announced on 24 Nov depends on FitzWalter's vote. That keeps this finding moderate and the range wide.
findings.independence: Interims 14 May 2026 set the 1.5x trigger (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/auction-technology-group--atg/interim-results-/9567577); FitzWalter's statement that it 'will support a buyback proposed by the Board, as led by the new Chair' (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/prn/auction-technology-group--atg/members-statement/9840285); the AGM poll on Resolution 17 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/auction-technology-group--atg/result-of-agm/9377369)

findings.why_not_priced: The board has said only that it will provide 'further detail on the outlook for FY2027' on 24 Nov. No board-led review has been signalled, and the 13 Nov circular simply recommends AGAINST. A priced board concession would show as a held rally. Instead the stock has given back the whole post-requisition move.
